---
name: handoff
description: >-
  Save a handoff of the current task so a new session (another account, another agent, or
  tomorrow) can continue without the user re-explaining. Use when the user wants to stop, switch
  account, is running out of usage or quota, or says "handoff", "save context", "wrap up for the
  next session", "bàn giao", "lưu ngữ cảnh", "sắp hết quota", "đổi tài khoản", "lưu lại để làm
  tiếp".
argument-hint: "[title]"
allowed-tools: Bash(cairn save *) Bash(cairn share *)
---
<!-- generated by scripts/gen_plugin.py from src/agent_cairn/assets — do not edit -->
Write a handoff for the work in THIS conversation and save it with `cairn save`, in one turn.

Rules:
- Write the handoff in English. Reply to the user in the language they are using.
- Be concrete: file paths, commands, error messages, decisions and WHY. Record approaches that
  failed so they are not retried. `Next steps` is an ordered checklist the next agent can start
  on immediately.
- Never include secrets, tokens or large code blocks; reference file paths instead.
- If an `ARGUMENTS:` line follows these instructions, use its text as the title.
- Task: if the work is about a ticket or task id (for example `PROJ-268`, from the conversation or
  the session name), pass it as `--task <id>`; otherwise leave `--task` out. Saving again with
  the same task replaces the older handoff of that task.
- Workspace: list every worktree and pipeline/run directory this task uses, with paths relative
  to the project directory, so the next session knows where to continue and cairn can check
  them for changes.
- The next session has none of this conversation. Before writing, scan the whole conversation
  for what it would otherwise have to rediscover or ask again:
  - instructions the user gave that still apply (work mode, test policy, writing style, how to
    address people, UI rules): put them under `User rules & preferences`, quoted briefly;
  - how to bring the work back up (data source and why, services, ports, logins to redo, launch
    commands, ids of stopped background runs): put them under `Environment / how to run`;
  - who made each decision (the user, the PO with a comment id or link, a reviewer).
- Paths: write them relative to the project directory; for files outside it, start with `~/`,
  never with your home directory spelled out. Under `Key files` list every file the next agent
  needs, including notes, tickets, evidence and other files git does not track: `cairn share`
  attaches the ones git does not carry. Put pull request links (number and URL) in
  `Current state` or `Workspace`.
- Never point at paths that only exist for this session (scratchpad, /tmp/claude-...): copy the
  file into the project first (for example the pipeline folder) and point there. cairn warns
  about such paths.

Steps:
1. Fill the template below from this conversation. Replace every `<...>` and remove the
   `<!-- -->` hints. The three sections marked required must have real content.
2. Run exactly this, with the filled template between the markers:

   ```bash
   cairn save --dir "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}" --agent claude-code --session ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} --task <id> <<'CAIRN_EOF'
   <filled template>
   CAIRN_EOF
   ```

3. Exit code 3 means the handoff was rejected. Each stderr line is `line N: rule: message`
   (line numbers count from the first line of the template). Fix every reported problem and
   run step 2 again. Stop after 3 attempts and show the user the remaining lines verbatim.
4. If the user wants to send this handoff to someone else (another person, another machine),
   also run `cairn share --dir "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}" <task or saved id>`. It writes a
   `.cairn.tgz` bundle without the user's local paths, with untracked files and uncommitted work
   attached. If it refuses because of secrets, show the listed lines and ask before adding
   `--redact`. Tell the user the bundle path, any `warning:` lines (for example a commit that is
   not pushed), and that the receiver runs `cairn import <file>` then `/cairn:resume <task>`.
5. On success, reply in at most 2 lines: the saved id (and the bundle path if shared), and the
   first next step.

Template:

```markdown
# <short title of the task>

## Goal
<!-- required: what the user wants and what "done" means (tests, behaviour) -->

## Current state
<!-- required: what is finished, half-done or broken right now -->

## Next steps
<!-- required: ordered checklist the next agent can start on immediately -->
- [ ] <first step>

## Decisions
<!-- each decision, its reason, and who made it (user, PO with a link or comment id, reviewer);
the next agent must not change it without asking -->

## Tried / didn't work
<!-- approaches that failed and why, so they are not retried -->

## User rules & preferences
<!-- instructions the user gave in this conversation that still apply, quoted briefly:
work mode (e.g. "fix fast, no unit tests"), writing style, how to address people, UI rules -->

## Environment / how to run
<!-- how to bring the work back up: where data comes from and why (e.g. which DB dump),
services and ports, logins the user must redo, launch commands, ids of stopped runs -->

## Open questions
<!-- questions only the user can answer -->

## Key files
<!-- paths that matter, one per line; for files in a temporary worktree give repo, branch
and PR instead, since the worktree may be deleted -->

## Workspace
<!-- one "- label: value" per line; cairn checks worktree and pipeline paths, e.g.
- worktree: .worktrees/proj-268-app
- pipeline: .pipeline/PROJ-268
- db: app_db_proj_268 -->
```
